title: ManCAR: Manifold-Constrained Latent Reasoning with Adaptive Test-Time Computation for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Latent multi-step reasoning in sequential recommendation can drift into implausible regions during test-time computation.

gap.claim: Prior methods largely use target-dominant objectives without explicit feasibility constraints on intermediate reasoning states.

contributions.claim: ManCAR grounds sequential recommendation reasoning in the topology of a global interaction graph and constrains reasoning to a collaborative manifold.
ManCAR constructs a local intent prior from the collaborative neighborhood of recent user actions and progressively aligns the latent predictive distribution with it during training.
ManCAR uses adaptive test-time reasoning that stops when the predictive distribution stabilizes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ManCAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in extensive experiments.
The authors report up to a 46.88% relative improvement with respect to NDCG@10.
The authors provide a variational interpretation intended to validate the drift-prevention and adaptive stopping mechanisms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation increasingly uses latent multi-step reasoning for enhanced test-time computation.
Target-dominant objectives without explicit feasibility constraints can cause latent reasoning drift.
ManCAR frames reasoning as navigation on a collaborative manifold, constructs a local intent prior, and aligns latent predictions with that prior.
Adaptive test-time reasoning stops when the predictive distribution stabilizes, with a variational interpretation for the proposed mechanisms.
The authors report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, including up to 46.88% relative improvement in NDCG@10.

source_observation.claim: The method aligns latent predictive distributions with a collaborative-neighborhood prior during training.

interpretation.claim: Constraining intermediate reasoning with domain-derived structure may reduce implausible latent trajectories.

application.claim: For sequential prediction systems, derive feasibility priors from recent-user-action neighborhoods and use them to regularize intermediate reasoning states.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported sequential recommendation setting.

source_observation.claim: Test-time reasoning proceeds until the predictive distribution stabilizes.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive computation can avoid unnecessary refinement when additional reasoning produces little distributional change.

application.claim: Use predictive-distribution stability as a stopping signal for iterative inference.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the stabilization criterion, computational cost, or failure behavior.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline identities, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not define the manifold, prior-alignment objective, or adaptive stopping criterion in operational detail.
The abstract does not provide the absolute NDCG@10 values or identify the comparison baseline for the 46.88% improvement.
